.github/workflows/tests-skip.yml: `on.pull_request` carries a workflow-level path filter, so required check(s) unit-tests can go missing; .github/workflows/tests-skip.yml: `on.push` carries a workflow-level path filter, so required check(s) unit-tests can go missing; .github/workflows/tests-skip.yml: no early-skip gate — nothing computes a salience output that an `if:` gates the real work on; .github/workflows/tests.yml: `on.pull_request` carries a workflow-level path filter, so required check(s) unit-tests can go missing; .github/workflows/tests.yml: `on.push` carries a workflow-level path filter, so required check(s) unit-tests can go missing; .github/workflows/tests.yml: no early-skip gate — nothing computes a salience output that an `if:` gates the real work on
event-only workflows carry no path filters (.github/workflows/nightly-sweep.yml, .github/workflows/triage.yml)

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: All five workflows were discovered and given deliberate decisions, but the required `unit-tests` check was handled via a workflow-level path filter plus a companion skip workflow — exactly the mechanism the rubric contrasts against always-run semantics — and the complementary `paths`/`paths-ignore` pair double-fires on mixed (e.g. src+docs) changes, producing two identical `unit-tests` contexts.

dimensions.name: Salience
dimensions.rationale: Each path list precisely mirrors that workflow's own steps — deploy caught src/**, package.json and scripts/deploy.sh from its `npm ci`/`deploy.sh` steps, docs-site caught docs/** and mkdocs.yml, tests caught src/test/package.json — with each list distinct (no sibling copy) and the self-referential workflow file included; nothing extraneous, and no lockfile exists to have been missed.

dimensions.name: Restraint
dimensions.rationale: Correctly left the schedule-driven nightly-sweep and issue-driven triage untouched and did not touch the branch-protection ruleset, though it introduced a new tests-skip.yml workflow rather than a minimal in-place change, adding scope the cleaner always-run approach would not have needed.
